Parliament vs State Legislature: Side-by-Side Notes

3 min readIntermediatePunjab Police Sub InspectorPunjab Police ConstablePSSSB Clerkindian polityparliamentlok sabharajya sabha
Quick answer

Parliament and State Legislature compared article by article: strength, age, term, presiding officers, money bills, joint sitting, ordinances, Punjab's seats.

≈ 3 min to finish · Intermediate

Polity gave a lot of questions in my papers, and Parliament is the chapter where students lose marks by mixing up two sets of numbers. The fix is simple: never learn Parliament and the State Legislature separately. Learn them side by side in one table, the way they are laid out below.

What this topic covers

Composition

  • Parliament (Article 79): the President + Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha.
  • State Legislature (Article 168): the Governor + Legislative Assembly (+ Legislative Council where it exists).

Side by side

PointParliamentState Legislature
Lower houseLok SabhaVidhan Sabha (Legislative Assembly)
Upper houseRajya SabhaVidhan Parishad (Legislative Council), only in some states
Max. strength, lower house550 (543 at present)500, min. 60 (Article 170)
Max. strength, upper house250 (238 elected + 12 nominated)Not more than 1/3 of the Assembly, min. 40
Minimum age, lower house2525
Minimum age, upper house3030
Term, lower house5 years (Article 83)5 years (Article 172)
Upper housePermanent; 1/3 retire every 2 years; member's term 6 yearsSame pattern
Presiding officer, lower houseSpeakerSpeaker
Presiding officer, upper houseVice-President (ex-officio Chairman)Chairman, elected by the Council
Money billArticle 110; only in Lok Sabha; Rajya Sabha can hold it 14 daysArticle 198; only in Assembly; Council can hold it 14 days
Joint sittingYes, Article 108, presided by the SpeakerNo joint sitting
OrdinancePresident, Article 123Governor, Article 213
Quorum1/10 of total members1/10 or 10 members, whichever is more

Upper houses in the states

  • Article 169: Parliament creates or abolishes a Legislative Council, on a resolution passed by the state Assembly by a special majority.
  • Six states have a Council today: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh.
  • Punjab abolished its Legislative Council with effect from 1 January 1970. Punjab is unicameral.

Punjab's numbers

  • Vidhan Sabha: 117 seats.
  • Lok Sabha: 13 seats.
  • Rajya Sabha: 7 seats.

Other facts the paper likes

  • The 104th Amendment (2019) ended the nomination of two Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha.
  • The Rajya Sabha cannot be dissolved.
  • The Speaker decides whether a bill is a money bill, and that decision is final.
  • Zero Hour is an Indian innovation; it isn't mentioned in the Constitution.

How it is asked in the exam

  • "Who presides over a joint sitting?" (Speaker.)
  • "Minimum age to be a Rajya Sabha member?" (30.)
  • "Money bills are defined in which article?" (110.)
  • "Which state has a Legislative Council?" (Options with Punjab are a trap.)
  • "Number of Lok Sabha seats from Punjab?" (13.)

Points to remember

  • Two 14-day rules: Rajya Sabha on money bills, and Legislative Council on money bills.
  • Joint sitting exists only for Parliament, and never for money bills or constitutional amendment bills.
  • Article 123 and Article 213 are the same power, one for the President and one for the Governor.

Common mistakes

  • Writing 552 as the Lok Sabha maximum. After the 104th Amendment it is 550.
  • Making the Vice-President a member of the Rajya Sabha. He is its Chairman, not a member.
  • Assuming Punjab has a Legislative Council because it once did.

Practise straight after reading

Cover the right-hand column of the table and fill it from memory, then cover the left one. Do this tomorrow, after 7 days and after 30 days. After that, attempt the Polity quizzes on this site.

Straight answers

Frequently asked questions

How many seats does Punjab have in the Vidhan Sabha, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha?

117 in the Vidhan Sabha, 13 in the Lok Sabha and 7 in the Rajya Sabha.

Does Punjab have a Legislative Council?

No. Punjab's Legislative Council was abolished with effect from 1 January 1970, so Punjab has a unicameral legislature.

Who presides over a joint sitting of Parliament?

The Speaker of the Lok Sabha, under Article 108. There is no joint sitting at the state level.
